content:
A recent PR has raised the possibility of making Qq available in Batteries. This is interesting since Qq is an extremely useful tool. Both Qq and Batteries currently depend on nothing. I've checked with @Joscha Mennicken whether that would cause maintenance issues downstream and they said the impact would be small and manageable.

It's been an implied principle that Batteries would always have no dependencies. Should we change "no dependencies" to "as few dependencies as possible"? Or to "just Qq"? Or stay with no dependencies at all?

cc: @Yaël Dillies @Wrenna Robson
I don't think I truly understand what Qq does (and what the gain is).
Qq is in the unfortunate situation of being both extremely useful (to write code faster and make it more maintainable) while being poorly supported by core and almost unmaintained
That does to me sound like we shouldn't include it in Batteries.

I would totally understand if I were asked to translate the existsAndEq code from Qq to core primitives, but I hope this doesn't become the standard when upstreaming: we eventually need core to provide a Qq-like framework

Yaël Dillies said:

I would totally understand if I were asked to translate the existsAndEq code from Qq to core primitives, but I hope this doesn't become the standard when upstreaming: we eventually need core to provide a Qq-like framework

Or for Batteries to provide an actively maintained Qq.
Yes I suppose that would be a better solution but it's a bigger ask.

It seems the reason why this Qq-like framework hasn't been provided by core so far is that people at the FRO manipulate relatively simple types while metaprogramming (few arguments, almost no typeclasses around) and therefore could get away using match_expr and alike
This simply does not scale to mathlib

Yaël Dillies said:

It seems the reason why this Qq-like framework hasn't been provided by core so far is that people at the FRO manipulate relatively simple types while metaprogramming

I think it would be more accurate to say that we don't know how to write a Qq-like framework that is robust enough to be included in core.
There's also no indication in this RFC of why one would want this. Without specific goals, it's hard to evaluate the question. Is there a reason to be adding tactics that rely on Qq to Batteries?
Yeah, again, what I would like is some concrete examples of possible gains.

Kim Morrison said:

There's also no indication in this RFC of why one would want this. Without specific goals, it's hard to evaluate the question. Is there a reason to be adding tactics that rely on Qq to Batteries?

This was brought up in an actual PR discussion. I don't want to bring up that particular discussion since that always strays the discussion into fixing that particular application rather than discussing the general issue.
Or put another way, it has concretely come up that there are tactics that might want to be upstreamed, but their use of Qq is an implementation detail that causes porting friction.

Okay, if it's a general issue without any specifics, then no, I think we should definitely not add Qq as a dependency to Batteries, it would encourage people to write tactics in Batteris using Qq, that probably should live elsewhere. :-)

François G. Dorais said:

Yaël Dillies said:

I would totally understand if I were asked to translate the existsAndEq code from Qq to core primitives, but I hope this doesn't become the standard when upstreaming: we eventually need core to provide a Qq-like framework

Or for Batteries to provide an actively maintained Qq.

If this suggestion is for batteries to absorb Qq, this doesn't sound particularly desirable to me either.

My understanding is that Qq defeq matching (~q()) is the main reason to discourage Qq—that, generally, defeq matches are not performant, and so we should avoid integrating them upstream if possible. Also worth mentioning that Qq suffers from a lot of ergonomic roughness.

In a future where Qq (also? instead?) provides a performant, non-defeq, match_expr style match (and/or more surgical defeq checking within such a match)—and where Qq is generally more actively maintained—I wonder if the conversation about it being upstream of (specific parts of?) batteries might go differently. :) I agree that as things stand it would not be great to put Qq so high in our ecosystem's hierarchy.
It appears that the general consensus is to not have Qq as a dependency and keep Batteries as depending on nothing.
